analysis.title: Parsing the 13F reports
key_insights: Q3 2026 13F filings show continued differentiation in hedge fund positioning. Tech had the largest increase in reported sector allocation (+0.9 points), yet hedge funds remain substantially underweight Tech versus the S&P 500. Hedge fund industry AUM was about USD 3.8 trillion at quarter-end.

Q3 was marked by Tech volatility, higher financing costs and rotation. July saw a sharp reversal in AI-linked stocks amid scrutiny of valuations, AI capex and funding needs. Middle East conflict and disrupted energy flows pushed oil, inflation concerns and yields higher.

Tech recovered in August on resilient activity and earnings, then rotated lower again in September as energy costs and yields rose. Higher financing costs weighed on rate-sensitive and smaller companies, leaving market leadership uneven.
Hedge funds lagged US equities in Q3: HFRX Global Hedge Fund Index -0.8% versus S&P 500 +2.0%. Gains were concentrated in a narrow group of strategies.

Cryptocurrency strategies led at +25.6% as Bitcoin gained about 44%, despite higher Treasury yields. Commodity Hedge +7.2%, Activist +7.1% and CTAs +6.0% also did well. Distressed Debt was weakest at -7.1%, followed by Fixed Income Arbitrage -1.2% and Equity L/S -0.6%.

Sector allocation changes in reported hedge fund longs: Tech +0.9 points, Healthcare and Energy +0.3, Communication Services and Financials +0.2. Industrials fell 0.8 points, Consumer Discretionary 0.5, Materials 0.2. The S&P 500 IT index rose 7% in Q3, so part of the Tech increase is market performance rather than net buying.

Aggregate active weight versus the S&P 500 rose from 27.0% at end-2025 to 31.1% in Q1 and 33.6% in Q2, then eased to 32.3% in Q3. It remains near its highest since 2012 and well above 2017-2025 levels.

Hedge fund Tech allocation is 22.4% against a 39.7% S&P 500 weight, a 17.3 point underweight and the largest relative sector position. Healthcare is the largest overweight (+3.1 points), then Industrials (+2.3), Materials (+2.0) and Financials (+1.6). Consumer Staples (-1.4) and Communication Services (-0.9) are underweight.

The Tech underweight has widened since 2022. Before 2022 it ranged from neutral to about 6 points below the index. Pictet attributes the gap to a structural rise in Tech's index weight that hedge fund allocations have not matched, not to an outright withdrawal.

Insider buying is returning in Tech. The S&P 500 insider buyer/seller ratio kept declining after the end of September, but the Tech ratio shows a marked resurgence in insider buying in November alongside the sector's decline, consistent with past dip-buying behaviour.
HFRX Global Hedge Fund Index beta to MSCI World rose to about 0.58 in early 2026, fell sharply and recovered only partially. It stayed below the peak through Q3 despite strong global equities.

Manager moves show disagreement within Tech. Point72 added Microsoft, Celestica and Intel and cut Credo, ASML and TSMC. Citadel added Cloudflare and cut Nvidia and Microsoft. Renaissance added Micron and AMD and cut Palantir and TSMC. Several managers also reduced broad-market ETF holdings.

The 25 largest hedge fund long holdings stay Tech-dominated: Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft lead, then SpaceX and Apple. Microsoft's market value rose 35% on a 37.5% stock gain while the reported position fell 2%. Nvidia's value rose 16% with the position up only 2%.

Largest position changes among top-25 holdings: Intel +83%, Meta +11%. Reductions: SanDisk -24%, AMD -15%, Micron -10%, Apple -9%. In S&P 500 ETFs, iShares Core fell 47%, Vanguard rose 38% and SPDR rose 2%, which points to rotation between vehicles.

Biggest position increases (holdings above USD 1B) extended beyond Tech. ARK Innovation ETF led and Utilities Select Sector SPDR rose 210%. Industrials: Honeywell Aerospace +158%, GFL Environmental +156%, Cummins and Curtiss-Wright +103%, Sunbelt Rentals +100%. Tech: NXP +116%, Shopify +89%, Intel +83%.

Biggest position reductions (above USD 1B remaining): Medline -68%, iShares Core S&P 500 ETF -47%. Industrials: Lockheed Martin -38%, Bloom Energy -37%, Republic Services -35%, Otis -34%, 3M -32%. Tech: Nebius -41%, NetApp -37%, STMicroelectronics -34%, Qualcomm -33%, Zoom -31%.
New initiations by number of managers: Medtronic and Meta each had seven managers (about USD 3.7B and USD 2.7B), Intel six (about USD 2.7B).

Full exits by number of managers: SpaceX six (about USD 2.4B), SPDR S&P 500 ETF four (about USD 2.0B), Applied Materials four (about USD 1.9B), Microsoft four (about USD 1.2B). Microsoft was newly added by five managers while four exited, and SpaceX was initiated by three and exited by six.
13F filings cover long US equity holdings only, carry no short positions and are published with a delay, so they are a backward-looking snapshot.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech had the largest increase in hedge fund sector allocation (+0.9 points), Intel was up 83%, and seven managers initiated Meta. Tech insiders have started buying again in November.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds remain 17.3 points underweight Tech, part of the allocation rise is the sector's 7% price gain, and managers cut Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Micron and Apple. SpaceX was exited by six managers and Microsoft fully exited by four.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Pictet says the 13F data cannot show how much of the Tech increase came from active buying, so the bullish read is not established by the filings.

theme_stances.key_argument: Technology remained central to portfolio activity, but Q3 data show selective repositioning and disagreement rather than broad-based increase in exposure.
theme_stances.evidence: substantial disagreement rather than a broad-based increase in Technology exposure

theme_stances.key_argument: As Tech has come under pressure, sector insiders have started buying again.
theme_stances.evidence: as Tech has come under pressure, sector insiders have started buying again
